title: Protocol Compatibility Matrix and Backpressure Contract for Hybrid Streaming + Transactional Pagination
creator: Jordan Patel
description: PRD to define an explicit wire-level compatibility matrix and runtime contract that unifies hybrid streaming APIs (server push + client-driven cursors) with transactional pagination and idempotent retries across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Purpose: avoid divergent client behaviors during rollouts, enable safe cross-language fallbacks, and provide observable signals for backpressure and degradation so product teams can reason about SLOs and cost impact.
goals: Define a single authoritative protocol document covering: message framing, cursor semantics, idempotency token usage, streaming termination codes, and out-of-band metadata for backpressure.
Specify language-level SDK contracts for Python/TS/Go that express the same developer ergonomics while mapping to the protocol differently as required by runtime idioms.
Provide exhaustive compatibility matrix for existing server versions and recommended client adapters, including migration path and downgrade strategy.
Create acceptance tests and CI gates that validate cross-language behavioral parity for pagination+streaming+retries scenarios.
requirements: Wire protocol: clear frame types for: DATA, CURSOR_UPDATE, HEARTBEAT, ACK, NACK, BACKPRESSURE_SIGNAL, END, ERROR with canonical numeric codes and human-readable message field.
Cursor semantics: cursors must be opaque tokens; server guarantees monotonic progression per partition; clients must support 'seek-to-offset' and explicit 'checkpoint' semantics.
Idempotency: every mutating pagination request that can be retried must carry an idempotency token; tokens must be replay-safe for 7 days by default.

Backpressure: define two-tier backpressure signals — SOFT (request client to slow polling/consume) and HARD (server will enqueue/defer and may return 429-like code). SDKs must expose these as observable events and hooks.
Streaming termination: clients must handle clean END frames and error frames including retryable vs non-retryable classification; streaming reconnection must honor resume cursors where available.
Retry policy: default cross-language retry policy must be documented (exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts=5 for idempotent ops, non-idempotent ops must fail fast unless explicit flag set).

Pagination atomicity: provide a transactional API for multi-page reads where a logical snapshot can be requested; specify server contract for consistency and client-side fallbacks if snapshot unavailable.
Observability mapping: SDKs must emit standardized metrics and trace attributes for: tokens_consumed, pages_fetched, stream_reconnects, backpressure_events, idempotent_retries, last_cursor_offset.

Compatibility matrix: list earliest server builds that support all frame types and behaviors; SDKs must implement runtime detection and feature negotiation to select fallback behavior when interacting with older servers.
Documentation: PRD must include code snippets for Python/TS/Go showing idiomatic usage for streaming+pagination, explicit examples of backpressure handling and recommended retry wrappers.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical protocol doc committed to the repo describing frame types, numeric codes, and full field schema.
Three language SDK proposals (Python, TypeScript, Go) with code examples that compile and pass linting and initial unit tests.
Automated cross-language integration tests in CI that exercise: streaming with resume, transactional pagination snapshot, idempotent retry scenarios, and soft/hard backpressure flows.
Compatibility matrix published in the docs site showing server-client mappings and a clear migration checklist for customers.
SDKs emit the standardized metrics; dashboard prototype in Console showing those metrics for a synthetic workload.
Performance guardrails validated: streaming resume latency under 200ms 95th percentile in test harness when using recommended client adapters.
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of existing SDKs to a new major version — this initiative focuses on defining contracts and adapters, not forcing immediate major bumps.
New transport protocol implementations beyond current HTTP/HTTP2/GRPC paths — experimentation can happen in parallel but not required for acceptance.
Server-side autoscaling policies; only client-server behavioral contracts are in scope.
risks: Divergence in language idioms could lead to different developer ergonomics and subtle bugs if the contract is ambiguous.
Backward compatibility gaps with older server clusters may cause increased error rates for customers during rollout.
Observable metrics may be misinterpreted; need clear naming and dashboards to avoid false positives.
implementation_notes: Work with Eng runtime team to finalize numeric frame codes and server feature flags for negotiation.
Create a lightweight adapter layer in each SDK that maps protocol frames to language-native iterators/async iterables/streams.
Prioritize Python and TypeScript SDKs for initial integration tests, then add Go once server-side negotiation is stable.
Eng to provide a test server mode that can simulate BACKPRESSURE_SIGNAL and snapshot-unavailable conditions for deterministic CI tests.
milestones: 2026-03-18: Protocol draft PR and initial review with Eng/runtime and SDK leads.
2026-03-25: SDK adapter design proposals and code snippets for Python/TS submitted.
2026-04-01: Integration test harness in CI with simulated server modes.
2026-04-05: Final PRD sign-off and publish compatibility matrix and migration guide.
notes: Aligns with long-running client compatibility initiative (see parent PM-224999) but targets hybrid streaming + transactional pagination as a discrete deliverable.
Recommend flagging security_review_required if idempotency token storage or replay windows change in downstream server work.
